stages.title: Elasticity of demand
stages.sub: After this, the student can classify PED and YED values and use them to predict revenue and the type of good.

steps.q: A café raises the price of coffee by 10% and the quantity sold falls by 40%. Compared with the size of the rise in price, is the fall in quantity bigger or smaller?

steps.q: Insulin has almost no substitutes, so a price rise barely changes the quantity bought. A well-known snack brand has many close substitutes, so a small price rise sends buyers elsewhere. Which good has the more elastic demand?
steps.right: The snack brand with many substitutes
steps.hint: Elastic demand means buyers can easily switch away when price rises.

steps.q: For that own-brand pasta, income rose 20% but quantity bought fell 5%. What single measure would capture how quantity demanded responds to a change in income?
steps.right: The percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in income
steps.wrong: The percentage change in income divided by the price of pasta
steps.hint: You want quantity's response relative to the income change that caused it.
